$comment: Alternative verifier configuration (run it with --template verify.oid4vp-1final-verifier-x509-san-dns): signed request objects with an x509_san_dns client id. Inji Verify signs them with Ed25519 (EdDSA), and suite release-v5.3.1 cannot verify an EdDSA request object against its x5c certificate, so every module stops at ValidateRequestObjectSignatureAgainstX5cHeader before the presentation (measured 2026-10-14). Kept to show that gap; the default template tests the presentation checks.

client.$comment: x509_san_dns: the suite adds the prefix itself and compares the result with the request's client_id. The host is the SAN of the certificate pki-init issues for Inji Verify's request signing key (compose/pki/generate.py, PKI_VERIFY_HOST).

credential.$comment: Private JWK with x5c the suite signs the presented SD-JWT VC with. Inji Verify takes the issuer key from x5c, so no trust setup is needed.

review.$comment: Verdict Inji Verify must show for a module the suite ends in REVIEW: the presented credential is valid unless the module tampers with it.
